answer: Stake deposits gate each voyage into the network, so every agent identity locks real capital upfront. Sybil attackers must scatter dune-like clouds of fake nodes, but each forged grain burns stake faster than it earns, while honest agents compound reputation inside a haven of attested history. Bottleneck lands on the attacker: capital scales linearly with every fake identity, yet reputation cannot, so cost of pretending eventually swallows any payoff from multiplying selves.
